# Akira - Full Reference

> Last updated: 2026
> Akira is a Discord card collecting bot for small friend groups. This file is the complete technical and design reference intended for LLM consumption. All features, mechanics, thresholds, and design decisions are documented here.

---

## What is Akira?

Akira is a curated Discord card collecting bot inspired by Karuta. Unlike Karuta, which pulls from every anime ever made, Akira's card pool is hand-picked by the server - only characters from shows the friend group actually watches. This removes the friction of sifting through thousands of irrelevant cards and makes every drop feel meaningful.

Akira has a warm, human-like personality. The bot is referred to as Akira and speaks in first person in all responses. Example: "Akira couldn't find that character" rather than "Error: not found". This is intentional - the human name and personality create emotional attachment and make the bot feel like a presence rather than a tool.

---

## Card System

### What a card is
A character can have several images. The primary image is the base variant (`id` ending in `-base`). Any other image is an alternate art. Players do not own templates. A grabbed card is an instance with:
- Character name and series
- Which image (variant)
- Frame (decorative border, cosmetic; drops use frame 0 until frame cosmetics exist)
- Print number (assigned when the card is claimed; lower means earlier)
- Quality (`COMMON`, `UNCOMMON`, `RARE`, `EPIC`, `LEGENDARY`)
- Dye (optional cosmetic tint; not built yet)
- Tag and alias (not built yet)
- Obtained date and timestamp

### Drop odds
Two separate rolls:

- Which art. Every base image has weight 100, so one character's base is as likely as another's. A base stays in that pool even if its rarity label says Rare (Kobeni's car is the current example). Alternate arts are harder: Rare weight 15, Secret Rare weight 3.
- Quality on that copy. Weights are Common 60, Uncommon 25, Rare 10, Epic 4, Legendary 1. Quality changes burn value. Only `LEGENDARY` is shown shiny. It does not change which picture was drawn.

### Card assets
Images are composed the first time a drop or a view needs them, then cached. Init does not pre-render the whole catalog. A cache miss composites character art under the frame and draws the name and print from `input/frames/{id}/config.json`.

- `normal.png` - static image
- `shiny.gif` - looping shimmer, used for Legendary (and dyed cards once dye exists)
- `burn.gif` - burn animation, composed when a card is burned

Discord does not animate APNG attachments, so shiny cards, burns, and a drop that contains a shiny card are GIF. A drop with no shiny cards stays a PNG.

Cached paths:
```
assets/cards/{variant_id}/{frame_id}/preview/none/normal.png
assets/cards/{variant_id}/{frame_id}/p{print}/none/normal.png
assets/cards/{variant_id}/{frame_id}/p{print}/none/shiny.gif
assets/cards/{variant_id}/{frame_id}/p{print}/none/burn.gif
```

Source art and frames live in:
```
input/characters/{series_slug}/{character_slug}/character.json
input/characters/{series_slug}/{character_slug}/{image}.png
input/frames/{id}/frame.png
input/frames/{id}/config.json
input/showcase/         ← reserved for a future Akira's Gift animation
```

### Frames
Dark (frame 0) and Yellow (frame 1) are the frames in the game. Prestige does not grant a frame. The showcase folder is unused.

---

## Commands

Slash commands and text commands call the same handlers. The text prefix defaults to `a` (`AKIRA_PREFIX` changes it). `adrop` and `a drop` are the same. The words after the command must be exactly the parameters that command accepts. Extra words are ignored. A character name may be several words. A card code or reminder action is one word. An optional user must be a Discord mention. The full command name always works. Short aliases are extra names. When an admin has enabled `aoverridekaruta`, that server also accepts `k` and `k!`.

### /drop
Parameters: none. Aliases: `d`.
Places cards in the configured drop channel as one picture. A normal drop is three cards. Quality over quantity makes it one. Four cards makes it four, and never five. If both are active, the drop is one card. Drop cooldown is 20 minutes, 10 with the shop or server reducer, and 5 when both are active. A prestige percent shortens that further. The drop stays open for 2 minutes. Unclaimed cards are not saved. For the first 20 seconds, if someone else grabs a card, the dropper can grab that same card and take it back. The message says they fought the other player off. The other player keeps their grab cooldown.

### Grab (reaction only)
No slash command and no alias. React 1️⃣ 2️⃣ or 3️⃣ on the drop. A four-card drop also accepts 4️⃣. A successful grab mints a 7 character card code, assigns the next print, and pays 5 bits. Grab cooldown is 5 minutes, 2 minutes 30 seconds with one reducer, and 1 minute 15 seconds with both. A prestige percent shortens that further. `av` with no code then opens that card.

### /collection [user] [filters]
Parameters: optional user mention. Optional filters. Aliases: `c`, `col`.
Lists owned cards, ten per page. Each line is code, stars, print, frame, series, and character.
Filters are `type:value` or `type is value`. `s` series, `c` character, `e` edition (1 is the base art), `t` tag, `q` quality from 1 common to 5 legendary, `o:#` low prints first, `o:w` most wishlisted first. A value runs until the next filter. `ac hello` is ignored.

### /view <card_id>
Parameters: `card_id` required on slash. Prefix `v` or `view` with no code uses the last grabbed card. Alias: `v`.
Shows the framed card, code, stars, print, frame, series, and character.

### /burn <card_id>
Parameters: required 7 character code. Alias: `b`.
Destroys an owned card and plays the burn animation. Bits: Common 10, Uncommon 25, Rare 50, Epic 100, Legendary 250.

### /lookup <name>
Parameters: `name` required on slash (character, series, or alias). Aliases: `lu`, `search`, `find`.
Numbered results, 25 per page, and a menu. Page buttons show the rest of the matches. Selecting one shows editions (card variants), a portrait, print count, and circulation. Buttons swap editions. Back returns to that results page. Prefix `alu` with no name opens that page for the last grabbed card, on the edition that was grabbed. `av` still shows the exact copy.

### /wishlist
`show` optional user. `add` required character. `remove` required character.
Aliases: `wl` (show, or the next word if it is add, remove, or show). Add: `wa`, `wish`, `wishadd`. Remove: `wr`, `wishremove`.
Wishlist slots are unlimited. Akira mentions the player when that character is in a drop.

### /daily
Parameters: none. No short alias (`adaily`).
Pays 100 bits plus `passiveBitsBonus`. Once every 24 hours.

### /cooldowns [user]
Parameters: optional user mention. Aliases: `cd`, `timers`.
Shows grab (5 minutes), drop (20 minutes), and daily (24 hours).

### /reminders [action]
Parameters: optional `action` of `daily`, `drop`, or `grab`. Aliases: `rm`, `remind`.
No action lists those three with a bell if the DM is on. An action toggles the DM for when that cooldown ends.

### /frame
`show` has no parameters. `default` requires a frame id and a server admin. `card` requires `card_id` and `action` (a frame id or `clear`). No short alias (`aframe`).
A null frame on a card uses `GuildConfig.defaultFrameId`.

### /userinfo [user]
Parameters: optional user mention. Aliases: `ui`, `whois`.
Bits, card count, prestige level, milestones this cycle, bits given this cycle, and any daily bonus already stored.

### /help and /ping
Parameters: none. No short aliases (`ahelp`, `aping`). Both save the Discord username used by WebUI sign-in.

### aoverridekaruta
Text only. No parameters. Server admin. Confirmation embed. Enabling also accepts `k` and `k!` in that server. Run it again to disable. Change Karuta's prefix before enabling.

### /give user card_id
Parameters: required `user` mention and required `card_id`. Alias: `g`.
Offers your card. Both players press the check mark before it moves. Either can cancel. Expires after 5 minutes.

### /trade user card_id their_card
Parameters: required `user`, `card_id`, and `their_card`. No short alias (`atrade`).
Offers your card for one of theirs. The image is the two cards with a swap arrow between them. Both players press the check mark. Either can cancel. Expires after 5 minutes.

### /tag tag_name [card_ids]
Parameters: required `tag_name`. Optional `card_ids`, space-separated 7 character codes. Alias: `t`.
No codes tags the last grabbed card. The emoji sits on the left of the card line. Untagged cards use ◾. `at the store` is not a command.

### /taglist [user]
Parameters: optional user mention. Aliases: `tags`, `tl`.
Lists that player's tags, each emoji, and how many cards use it.

### /tagcreate tag_name emoji
Parameters: required name and emoji. Aliases: `tagadd`, `ta`, `tc`.
Names are one word: letters, numbers, `-` and `_`. Server emojis are not allowed.

### /tagdelete tag_name
Parameters: required name. Aliases: `tagremove`, `tr`, `td`.
Deletes the tag and clears it from that player's cards. Giving or trading a card also clears its tag.

### /untag [card_ids]
Parameters: optional `card_ids`, space-separated 7 character codes. Alias: `ut`.
No codes untags the last grabbed card. The line goes back to ◾.

### /multiburn tag_name
Parameters: required `tag_name`. Alias: `mb`.
Burns every card on that tag. Asks first: the confirmation says how many cards and names the rarest. Cards in an open give or trade are left alone. Pays the same bits as burn.

### Not finished
These reply that the feature is not wired up. They take no parameters.
`/dye`, `/import`.

### /shop
Parameters: none. Aliases: `is`, `itemshop`.
Opens an embed of the first personal buff, with previous, next, and buy. There is no `/shop buy`. Buying starts a timer. Buying again extends the time left. The seven buffs are drop cooldown (400 bits, 24h, 10 minutes), grab cooldown (350, 12h, 2 minutes 30 seconds), burn value (300, 24h, `/burn` pays double), four cards (500, 24h), shiny luck (600, 24h, mints 1 in 51), featured series (450, 24h, that series is twice as likely and stays locked to the series shown at purchase), and quality over quantity (500, 24h, one card and main characters are much more likely).

### /pool
`show` or `give` with a required bit amount. `apool` is show. `apool give 200` moves 200 bits into the server pot and the player's milestone bar.

### /inventory
Parameters: none. Aliases: `i`, `inv`, `items`.
Lists shop, server, and prestige buffs separately, then a combined result. An empty source is omitted.

### /milestone
`show` or `claim`. Lists the ten steps. The first step is 250 bits and pays 200. Each step doubles, up to 128,000 bits paying 30,000. Claim pays the next step's bits and does not stamp a prestige percent.

### /prestige
Parameters: none. Always says how far the next milestone is and what waiting would add. After milestone 5 is claimed, a confirm button resets the bar and stamps permanents for every step past 5 that was claimed. Prestige at 5 keeps none. Prestige at 10 keeps all five percents. A second prestige at 10 makes each of those 2%. Cards, bits, tags, and frames stay. Daily bits do not increase.

---

## Economy

### Bits
Bits are the only currency. Grabbing pays 5. Daily pays 100, plus any bonus already stored on the profile, once every 24 hours. New prestiges do not add to daily. Burning one card pays 10, 25, 50, 100, or 250 by quality. Burn value doubles a single `/burn`. Multiburn pays the plain table.

Bits leave the wallet in two ways. The shop buys a personal timed buff. A pool gift enters the server pot and the giver's milestone bar. Shop purchases do not fill the bar. Cards, tags, and frames are never wiped by spending or prestiging.

### Shop
Seven personal buffs. Buying starts the clock. Buying the same one again adds the duration onto the time left. Featured series, burn value, and quality over quantity are shop-only.

A normal mint is 1 in 100 cards (legendary is the only shiny drop). Shiny luck from the shop or the server alone is 1 in 51. Both together is 1 in 34. Player-facing copy says those odds, not a weight.

Quality over quantity forces one card even if four cards is also active. Four cards never becomes five. Main characters are the AniList MAIN cast. Supporting characters, and characters with no role, can still drop.

### Server pool
One pot per server. At midnight UTC, if the pot is under 500 bits, nothing is applied and the bits stay. At 500 or more, the pot is spent to 0 and the chosen buff lasts 24 hours. The roll also runs at startup if that night was missed, and the result is announced in the drop channel.

The tier is the highest reached. One buff is chosen from that tier and every tier below it. Tier 4 chooses two different buffs from tiers 1 to 3.

| Tier | Bits | Choice |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | 500 | Grab cooldown, always |
| 2 | 2,000 | One of grab cooldown, drop cooldown, or shiny luck |
| 3 | 2,500 | One of those, or four cards |
| 4 | 5,000 | Two different buffs from the tier 3 list |

Shop and server cooldown reducers stop at 5 minutes for drop and 1 minute 15 seconds for grab. Shiny luck stops at 1 in 34. Prestige percents apply after those floors.

### Milestones
Only pool gifts fill the bar. Costs double. The payout is always less than the step. Leftover progress stays. Claim one step at a time. Claiming pays bits and does not grant the prestige percent.

| Step | Cost | Pays | Prestige after this |
|------|------|------|---------------------|
| 1 | 250 | 200 | |
| 2 | 500 | 350 | |
| 3 | 1,000 | 600 | |
| 4 | 2,000 | 1,000 | |
| 5 | 4,000 | 2,000 | Opens prestige. No percent. |
| 6 | 8,000 | 3,500 | Burns pay 1% more |
| 7 | 16,000 | 6,000 | Grab cooldown 1% shorter |
| 8 | 32,000 | 10,000 | Drop cooldown 1% shorter |
| 9 | 64,000 | 18,000 | Mints a little more likely |
| 10 | 128,000 | 30,000 | Main characters 1% more likely |

There is no step past 10.

### Prestige
Optional once milestone 5 is claimed. Confirming resets the bar and the claim count to 0 and stamps a permanent for every step past 5 that was claimed. Prestige at 5 stamps nothing. Prestige at 7 keeps the step 6 and step 7 percents. Prestige at 10 keeps all five. Each later prestige adds another 1% to every buff that prestige included, so two prestiges at 10 is 2% on all five.

`/prestige` always says the bits still to give and what waiting would add. Before step 5 there is no confirm button. Prestige does not grant a frame and does not add a daily bits bonus.

---

## Card Asset Pipeline (technical)

### Init phase
Runs once on setup or whenever new content is added:
1. Checks that frame folders and character art exist. It does not pre-render every combination.
2. Seeds the database with series, characters, and card variants
3. Registers Discord slash commands
4. Creates init.lock at start, deletes it on clean completion

Card images are composed later, on the first drop or view, and written into `assets/cards`.

### Run phase (the bot)
Lightweight. On startup checks for init.lock:
- If init.lock exists: comes online immediately, sets Discord status to "Akira is getting ready...", responds to all commands with a friendly waiting message. Uses fs.watchFile on the lock file to detect when init completes, then unlocks all commands and updates status.
- If init.lock does not exist: normal operation immediately.

### Animation design principles
- Shiny GIF: a diagonal band sweeps from the top-left to the bottom-right, brightening the art under it. The core of the band is white and the edges carry a light prismatic tint. The loop restarts after the band has left the card.
- Burn GIF: fade in, flames, fade out, then loop.
- Akira's Gift: not built. The reserved idea is a looping showcase reel.

---

## WebUI

A React frontend served both as a standalone browser site and as a Discord Activity (embedded within Discord itself). The same codebase handles both contexts.

### Auth: Discord Activity (inside Discord)
The @discord/embedded-app-sdk provides the user's Discord ID directly. No login screen is shown. The client sends an X-Discord-User-Id header with every API request. The Express backend trusts this header when the request originates from a Discord Activity iframe origin.

### Auth: Browser (outside Discord, e.g. at school on a network that blocks discord.com)
1. User enters their Discord username
2. Backend asks the bot to DM a one-time verification code to that Discord user
3. User enters the code on the site - proves they control that Discord account
4. First time: prompted to set a site password
5. Subsequent logins: Discord username + site password → session cookie

This flow avoids OAuth entirely. The browser never touches discord.com - only the bot server does, which is hosted at home and not subject to school network blocks.

### WebUI features
- Browse personal card collection
- View card details and animations
- Check bits balance
- Buy the seven shop buffs
- See the server pot, tonight's choices, and the live buffs, and give bits
- See the milestone bar and claim a step
- Prestige with the same confirm as Discord
- See shop, server, and prestige buffs with the combined sentences
- Stats rankings (the old leaderboard link opens Stats)
- Admin panel: manage card pool, trigger asset regeneration

---

## Database Models (Prisma SQLite)

- Series: id, name, slug
- Character: id, name, slug, seriesId, description, gender, aliases
- CardVariant: id, characterId, name, rarity (label for alternate-art weight; bases ignore it), image
- Card: id, variantId, frameId, printNumber, quality (COMMON through LEGENDARY), ownerId, tag, alias, dye, obtainedAt
- PrintCounter: variantId, nextPrint
- Drop: id, guildId, channelId, messageId, createdAt, expiresAt
- DropSlot: id, dropId, position (1-3), variantId, quality, frameId, claimedById, cardId
- GuildConfig: guildId, dropChannelId
- User: id, discordId, discordUsername, preferredName, passwordHash, bits, prestigeLevel, milestoneCount, milestoneProgress, passiveBitsBonus, isAdmin
- Wishlist: id, userId, characterId
- ServerPool: id, guildId, totalBits, lastReset, activeBuff, buffTier, buffExpiry
- UserPoolContribution: id, userId, guildId, bits, date
- Inventory: id, userId, itemType, quantity
- Cooldown: id, userId, type (enum: GRAB, DROP, DAILY), expiresAt

---

## Infrastructure

- Hosted on Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM64) at home
- Docker Compose with services: init, bot, webui-server, webui-client, docs
- Nginx Proxy Manager handles external routing
- SQLite database in a named Docker volume (akira-db)
- Cached card images in a named Docker volume (akira-assets)
- Source art in a named Docker volume (akira-input)
- Bot and webui-server share the akira-db volume
- Init service runs once and exits; bot depends on init completing successfully

---

## Design Decisions and Rationale

**Why curated card pool?**
Karuta's strength (thousands of characters) is a friction point for small groups. New players see cards from shows they've never heard of and feel no connection. A curated pool means every drop is relevant to someone in the server.

**Why unlimited wishlist slots?**
Karuta gates wishlist slots behind purchases. For a friend group bot this creates unnecessary friction for the exact players Akira is trying to onboard. Removing the cap costs nothing at small scale and removes a barrier to engagement.

**Why no black market, clans, or nodes?**
These systems require large player populations to function meaningfully. Black market needs volume for auctions. Clans and nodes need enough players for territory wars. Workers are an idle game mechanic that only pays off over a long grind. At friend group scale these systems feel hollow rather than engaging.

**Why single currency?**
Multiple currencies (bits, gems, tickets) create confusion and enable pay-to-win. For a friend group bot, simplicity and fairness matter more than monetisation levers.

**Why GIF for animations?**
Discord shows an APNG attachment as a still image. GIF attachments play. The palette is limited to 256 colours, which is the tradeoff for the shimmer and the burn to move in chat.

**Why compose cards on demand?**
Print numbers are only known when someone claims a card, and frames carry text positions for the name and print. Pre-rendering every variant, frame, and animation up front could not include that text, and it had to be redone whenever a frame changed. A cache miss is one composite. Repeat views read the file.

**Why SQLite over PostgreSQL?**
No separate database server to run or maintain. File-based, lives in a Docker volume, trivially backed up. At friend group scale there are no concurrent write patterns that SQLite cannot handle. Prisma makes migration to PostgreSQL straightforward if needed in future.

**Why the name Akira?**
A genuine Japanese name that fits the anime aesthetic naturally without feeling forced. Short, memorable, easy to type. Having a human name creates emotional attachment - users naturally refer to the bot in third person and feel like they are interacting with a presence rather than a utility.
